title: Phase 1: zod for runtime schema validation
decision: Use zod for ingredient JSON runtime validation in Phase 1. Chosen over ajv (heavier) and hand-rolled validation (error-prone). zod's .enum() guards map cleanly to the controlled vocabulary union types already defined in TypeScript.
rationale: zod is already idiomatic in Vite/React stacks, produces typed parse results, and its enum guards directly enforce the controlled vocabulary invariants without a separate JSON schema file to maintain.

title: Phase 1: seed fixture must exercise all converter branches
decision: The Phase 1 seed fixture (10-15 ingredients) must include at least one example of: a pairsWith group ref, a pairsWith direct ID ref, a cuisineWeights object, a populated cookMinutes, and a blank cookMinutes. This ensures every converter branch is proven before Phase 2 runs the full 119-ingredient catalog.
rationale: If untested converter branches hit only in Phase 2, debugging cost multiplies. Testing all branches on a small hand-crafted fixture is cheap and prevents late surprises.
